mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher interest rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals stronger economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates a tightening monetary policy to combat inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests strong labor market conditions, which can lead to wage inflation and higher interest rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases sharply and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS increases sharply and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which can lead to slower economic growth and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS is decreasing.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows below 2% year-over-year and industrial production (INDPRO) is stagnant, it signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 YoY < 2% and INDPRO is stagnant.
